hook: Wireless routers, full moons and timber wolves. The premise sounds like a pun, and the file carries it out with a completely straight face, right down to requiring an animal handler for every test. It is short, and the addendum is where the idea really gets going.
whyItMatters: It is a tidy example of the light, high-concept side of the wiki: take an old folklore pattern of moonlight and contagion and graft it onto household networking gear. The writing never winks at the reader; the comedy comes from procedures that treat the premise with full seriousness. That restraint is what keeps a one-joke idea readable to the end.
thingsToNotice: Notice the details that make the absurd feel managed: the three days of overlapping signal needed for spread, the wolf-per-square-meter figure, the Faraday cage. The addendum escalates by following the logic one careful step at a time, and its dates track successive full moons. The terse final sentence lands as a punchline precisely because everything before it was set up so methodically.
